newsitem.title: UK: GLYNWED DIPS, PROFITS UP BUT OUTLOOK WARY.
newsitem.headline: GLYNWED DIPS, PROFITS UP BUT OUTLOOK WARY.

text.p: Shares in UK engineering group Glynwed Plc were indicated slightly lower on Tuesday on a cautious outlook for the full year despite better than expected half-year results.
The shares were down 2-1/2p at 249-1/2p by 0725 GMT.
Glynwed's pre-tax profit figure of 43.9 million stg exceeded most analysts' expectations. Charterhouse Tilney analyst Michael Blogg, for instance, had forecast a pre-tax total of 40.5 million.
The group's pre-tax profit rose 9.2 percent on reduced turnover of 632 million. But a maintained dividend of 4.4p per share was slightly disappointing, analysts said.
"I would have expected them to increase the dividend because for the year as a whole I see dividend cover of about two times," said Blogg.

Meanwhile, Glynwed highlighted the adverse impact of the strong pound and of weak European market conditions. The company said the impact of currency changes was about four million stg but the lower contribution from exports was mostly offset by the buoyant domestic economy.
Glynwed remained cautiously optimistic about the rest of the year but added that the abolition of tax credits on dividend payments would raise the group's pension charge.

"There was progress in margins in all four of the group's divisions," Blogg said. "But the strong warning on the impact of sterling will keep forecasts under control and we don't have any idea of the likely size of the pension charge."
